verification_categories_derived_from_spe: DATA FRAME transmission with each DLC value 0..8.
REMOTE FRAME transmission + matching DATA FRAME response.
Multi-node bitwise arbitration (2 nodes, 3 nodes, identifier corner cases).
Arbitration loss + receiver-switch behavior.
DATA FRAME vs REMOTE FRAME same-ID priority (DATA wins).
CRC computation (polynomial X^15 + X^14 + X^10 + X^8 + X^7 + X^4 + X^3 + 1).
Bit-stuffing on/off in correct fields.
STUFF ERROR detection on 6 identical consecutive bits.
FORM ERROR detection on illegal bits in fixed-form fields.
BIT ERROR detection on transmitted vs monitored mismatch.
ACKNOWLEDGMENT ERROR detection on missing dominant ACK.
ACTIVE / PASSIVE ERROR FLAG generation + superposition behavior.
Error counter increment / decrement per Section 7 rules 1-12.
Fault confinement transitions: active → passive → bus-off → active (recovery).
Hard synchronization on SOF + resynchronization on subsequent edges (within RJW).
Bit timing per-segment programming (PROP_SEG / PHASE_SEG1 / PHASE_SEG2 / RJW / prescaler).
OVERLOAD FRAME generation (receiver-internal vs intermission-dominant cause).
Max 2 consecutive OVERLOAD FRAMEs rule.
INTERMISSION = 3 recessive bits enforcement.
Bus-off recovery after 128 × 11 consecutive recessive bits.
Sleep / wake-up cycle.
Section 9 oscillator-tolerance modifications (3rd-bit-of-INTERMISSION as SOF).
fields.notes: Bosch CAN 2.0 does not include a formal verification plan; categories above are derived from Sections 3-9. Industry-standard CAN-conformance test suites (e.g. ISO 16845) implement these scenarios programmatically.
